audit_boundary: Manual audit of Critique-origin verified review-issue clusters. Labels are cluster-level paper-readiness judgments from case-table evidence plus spot checks against paper-text snippets available in the run artifact; final paper claims should still be spot-checked against the original paper text.

clusters.label: B
clusters.claim_anchor: The model uses a Graph Convolutional Network (GrCN) architecture and implements shape conditioning.
clusters.inventory_or_quote: Inspired by the well-known ControlNet for conditioned image generation, supposing an unconditioned 3D molecule generative model was already trained as a prior model, then $\mathrm{Gr}\mathbf{CN}$ is designed to includ...
clusters.manual_decision: Keep as a defensible paper-facing concern with normalized wording.
clusters.raw_paper_evidence_checked: Paper text defines GrCN as including a 3D shape constrain/constraint module and a 3D molecule generation module; Figure 1 is described as the basic architecture of GrCN.
clusters.counterevidence_checked: Searches over the run artifact found no ablation section and no component-isolation ablation for the constrain/constraint module; only ShapeMol guidance variants were found under 'without'.
clusters.wording_caution: Normalize the target to '3D shape constraint/control module' and avoid treating the awkward phrase 'consisting of a constrain module' as the final paper wording.
clusters.reason: The target is a concrete central method component and no component ablation was found, but the extracted entity phrase is awkward and overlaps the broader Graph ControlNet/control-module concern.

clusters.label: B
clusters.missing_or_mismatch: acceptance prediction head; component-isolation ablation for trained acceptance prediction head
clusters.claim_anchor: SpecDec++ formulates the choice of candidate length K as a Markov Decision Process and provides theoretical analysis for its optimal policy.
clusters.inventory_or_quote: Compared with the baseline speculative decoding (SpecDec) with fixed candidate lengths, by adaptively determining the candidate lengths via a trained acceptance prediction head, \ours achieves a relative \textbf{7.2\%},
clusters.manual_decision: Keep as a defensible paper-facing concern with cautious attribution wording.
clusters.raw_paper_evidence_checked: Paper text repeatedly states that SpecDec++ uses a trained acceptance prediction head and attributes adaptive candidate-length speedups to it.
clusters.counterevidence_checked: Searches for ablation, without acceptance, and prediction-head ablation found no component-isolation ablation for the trained acceptance prediction head.
clusters.wording_caution: Frame this as an empirical attribution concern for the adaptive decoding component, not as a challenge to the MDP/theory itself.
clusters.reason: The component is concrete and central to the reported improvements, while the paper-text snippets do not show a corresponding ablation.

clusters.label: B
clusters.missing_or_mismatch: same-setting comparison against paper-named Graphormer baseline
clusters.claim_anchor: The proposed method achieves strong empirical performance, for example on substructure counting tasks measured by Mean Absolute Error (MAE).
clusters.inventory_or_quote: Extensive experiments verify these claims across synthetic datasets, graph property prediction datasets, and long-range graph benchmarks. Specifically, PST outperforms all baselines on QM9~\citep{QM9} dataset.
clusters.manual_decision: Keep as a defensible review concern with same-task caveat.
clusters.raw_paper_evidence_checked: Paper text names Graphormer in the discussion of graph transformers and reports Graphormer comparisons for some graph-property/LRGB contexts.
clusters.counterevidence_checked: The substructure-counting MAE table context lists expressive GNN baselines such as ID-GNN, NGNN, GNNAK+, I2-GNN, and PPGN; no Graphormer row was found for the same substructure-counting setting.
clusters.wording_caution: Phrase as missing same-task Graphormer/graph-transformer baseline for the substructure-counting MAE claim, not as absence of every Graphormer comparison in the paper.
clusters.reason: Graphormer is paper-named and relevant to the graph-transformer comparison space, but the verified claim is narrower than the full paper; the concern is usable only with the same-setting caveat.

clusters.label: B
clusters.missing_or_mismatch: same-setting comparison against paper-named PixelPick baseline; same-setting comparison against paper-named EqualAL baseline
clusters.claim_anchor: HALO outperforms key baselines (e.g., EqualAL, RIPU) in semantic segmentation under domain shift, as shown in Table 1c.
clusters.inventory_or_quote: HALO demonstrates a substantial improvement of +10.4\% compared to methods (a) and (b) in Table \ref{tab:main-ablation}.
clusters.manual_decision: Keep as a defensible paper-facing concern with protocol caveat.
clusters.raw_paper_evidence_checked: Paper text names PixelPick and EqualAL in active-learning semantic-segmentation related work, while HALO claims broad active/domain-adaptation improvements.
clusters.counterevidence_checked: Searches found PixelPick and EqualAL in related-work contexts but did not find them as rows in the reported result/baseline table snippets; RIPU appears repeatedly as an included comparator.
clusters.wording_caution: Say the paper omits PixelPick/EqualAL-style active-learning semantic-segmentation comparisons or adaptations; do not assert they are definitely identical-protocol ADA baselines.
clusters.reason: The omitted baselines are paper-named and close to the active-learning segmentation setting, but protocol comparability needs careful wording.
